md_description: Workflow for studying virus-host protein interactions during infection using affinity purification followed by mass spectrometry. Infected host cells are purified to enrich viral and host protein complexes, the captured spectra are processed into identified interaction features, and the resulting derived network supports analysis of host machinery hijacked by viruses and prioritization of antiviral drug targets.

infected_host_cell_culture.reasoning: For the infected_host_cell_culture Entity node, I included only intrinsic biological/source descriptors of the infected culture: host cell identity, virus identity, infection context, and origin of the culture. I excluded affinity purification parameters, mass spectrometry settings, raw signal/file properties, and computed interaction results because those belong to downstream Process, Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided sample/experiment identifiers if they would be repeated elsewhere, and I did not duplicate any already-generated fields (none were provided here).

md_schema.descr: Host cell line used as the biological substrate for infection, e.g. HEK293T, A549, Vero. Report the established line name at the point the infected culture is created; use the exact line designation used in the study.

Taxonomic species of the host cells for the infected culture, recorded as the organism of origin of the cell line, e.g. Homo sapiens, Mus musculus. This is an intrinsic property of the biological source, not a culture condition.

Virus used to infect the host cell culture, reported as the specific virus name or strain designation, e.g. Influenza A virus, SARS-CoV-2, EBV strain B95-8. Capture the infecting agent identity for the cultured biological source.

Virus strain, isolate, or variant used for infection, if distinguished from the general virus name; e.g. A/WSN/1933, Delta variant, laboratory isolate name. Record the exact designation used for the infected culture.

Categorical status indicating that the culture is infected at the time it is used as input to affinity purification. Use this field to distinguish infected cultures from mock-infected or uninfected controls.

Time elapsed from viral inoculation to harvest of the infected host cells, in hours, measured at the point the culture is collected for downstream affinity purification. Typical values are study-specific, commonly 1-72 h depending on virus and assay design.

Passage number of the host cell culture used for infection, recorded at the time the infected culture is established. This helps track biological consistency and should use the laboratory passage count (e.g. P5, P12).

Origin of the host cell culture used to generate the infected sample, for example primary cells, immortalized cell line, or patient-derived culture. This describes what the biological source is, not how it was processed.

affinity_purification_of_complexes.reasoning: For the affinity_purification_of_complexes Process node, I included only protocol and operation descriptors: purification strategy, bait/handle used, key reagent and wash/elution conditions, replication, and a process-quality indicator. I excluded biological source properties of the infected culture, capture/instrument details, raw file properties, and downstream identification/network outputs because those belong to the Entity, Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes respectively. No already_generated fields were provided, so I did not need to suppress overlaps with prior schema fields.

md_schema.descr: Affinity purification strategy used to enrich virus-host protein complexes from the infected cell culture, recorded at the point the purification is performed. Examples include immunoprecipitation, tandem affinity purification, FLAG pull-down, HA pull-down, or tagged bait pulldown.

Name of the viral or host bait protein used to capture associated complexes during the affinity purification step, e.g. viral nonstructural protein, tagged host interactor. Report the molecule targeted by the purification protocol.
Epitope or affinity tag used on the bait protein for purification, if applicable, e.g. FLAG, HA, GFP, Strep. Record the tag present at the purification step, not the downstream detection method.

Qualitative stringency level of the wash steps used during affinity purification, recorded during the protocol execution. Use a categorical description of how aggressively nonspecific binders were removed.

Method used to release purified protein complexes from the affinity matrix, recorded at the end of the purification step. Examples include competitive peptide elution, denaturation, low pH, or on-bead digestion.
Biological or technical replicate identifier for this affinity purification run, recorded at the time the purification is performed. Use a study-local integer such as 1, 2, or 3.

Operator-assessed outcome quality of the affinity purification step, captured after recovery of complexes and before mass spectrometry. Use this to summarize whether the eluate was sufficient and specific enough for downstream acquisition.

purified_protein_complex_fraction.reasoning: For the purified_protein_complex_fraction Entity node, I included only properties of the recovered enrichment material itself: fraction identity, physical form, concentration, volume, storage, and enrichment quality. I excluded purification protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded mass spectrometry acquisition settings, raw spectrum properties, and downstream computed interaction outputs because those belong to Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were supplied, so there was no overlap to suppress.

md_schema.descr: Type of recovered material obtained immediately after affinity purification, e.g. eluate, bead-bound fraction, or digest-ready fraction. Record what the purified protein complex fraction physically is at the point it enters mass spectrometry preparation.

Protein concentration of the purified complex fraction measured after recovery and before mass spectrometry loading, in micrograms per milliliter. Typical values are assay-dependent and often fall in the low ng/mL to mg/mL range depending on elution volume and enrichment efficiency.

Total volume of the purified protein complex fraction available after affinity purification, in microliters, measured at the point of transfer to downstream handling or instrument preparation. Typical values are usually in the 1-1000 uL range.

Condition used to hold the purified fraction before downstream acquisition, such as immediate use, refrigerated storage, or frozen storage. Record the state of the fraction at the time it is maintained between purification and measurement.

Qualitative assessment of how well the fraction is enriched for candidate virus-host complexes after affinity purification, judged before mass spectrometry. Use this to capture whether the recovered material is clean, concentrated, or visibly contaminated.

Total mass of protein recovered in the purified complex fraction, in micrograms, measured after enrichment and before instrument loading. Typical values depend on bait abundance and purification efficiency and are often in the 0.1-100 ug range.
Date the purified protein complex fraction was prepared or recovered from affinity purification, recorded as the calendar date of fraction generation prior to downstream acquisition.

mass_spectrometry_acquisition.reasoning: For the mass_spectrometry_acquisition Capture node, I included only instrument/session configuration and active acquisition settings: instrument identity, analyzer, ionization, scan range, resolution, polarity, acquisition mode, and run duration. I also included agent properties required for Capture nodes (manufacturer, model, serial number) and a session-level quality indicator. I excluded properties of the purified fraction, raw file format/size, and downstream identifications because those belong to the Entity, Signal, and Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so no overlap filtering was needed.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the mass spectrometer used for the acquisition session, recorded as the hardware vendor operating the instrument that generated the spectra. Example: Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bruker, Sciex.
Model name or series of the mass spectrometer used to record the spectra, captured for the acquisition session. Example: Orbitrap Fusion Lumos, Q Exactive HF, timsTOF Pro.
Instrument serial number for the mass spectrometer used in the acquisition, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware instance. Use the exact manufacturer serial identifier when available.

Ionization source configured for the acquisition session, recorded at the mass spectrometer before spectral collection. Examples include electrospray ionization or matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization.
Acquisition mode used to record spectra from the purified complex fraction, recorded during the run. Use this to distinguish full-scan, data-dependent, or data-independent collection strategies.
Primary mass analyzer used by the instrument during the acquisition session, e.g. Orbitrap, TOF, ion trap. Record the analyzer responsible for mass measurement in this run.
Lower bound of the m/z scan range recorded during spectral acquisition, in mass-to-charge units. Typical values are instrument- and method-specific and often lie within 50-4000 m/z.

Upper bound of the m/z scan range recorded during spectral acquisition, in mass-to-charge units. Typical values are instrument- and method-specific and often lie within 50-4000 m/z, and must be greater than mz_scan_range_start.

Mass spectrometer resolving power used for the acquisition session, reported at the reference m/z specified by the method or vendor setting. Common values are instrument-dependent and may range from 15,000 to 240,000 or higher.
Ion polarity used during the acquisition session, recorded as the instrument acquisition setting. For proteomics acquisitions this is typically positive mode.
Total elapsed acquisition time for the mass spectrometry run, in minutes, measured from the start to the end of spectral recording for this sample. Typical values are often 30-240 minutes.

Session-level qualitative indicator of whether the acquisition completed as intended and produced usable spectra. Use this after the run to mark obvious issues such as unstable spray, low signal, or aborted acquisition.

raw_ms_spectra.reasoning: For the raw_ms_spectra Signal node, I included only raw file and measurement-artefact descriptors: file format, file size, dimensionality, acquisition-to-file mapping, storage location, and technical quality metrics. I excluded instrument settings, sample properties, and derived identifications because those belong to Capture, Entity, and Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were supplied, so there were no field-name or semantic duplicates to suppress.

md_schema.descr: Digital file format of the raw mass spectral data as stored immediately after acquisition, e.g. mzML, mzXML, vendor RAW. Record the exact format of the raw artefact, not the instrument configuration.
Size of the raw spectral data file in bytes at the time of storage or ingestion into the workflow. Typical values are instrument- and run-dependent and may range from megabytes to tens of gigabytes.
Total number of spectra contained in the raw file, counted after acquisition and before any downstream processing. This describes the raw data volume represented by the signal artefact.

Number of acquisition channels or parallel data streams represented in the raw file, if applicable to the instrument output. Use this only when the file structure explicitly contains multiple channels.
Storage location or URI of the raw spectral file, recorded for retrieval of the unprocessed artefact. Examples include file paths, object store URIs, or repository accessions.
MD5 checksum of the raw spectral file, recorded to verify integrity of the stored signal artefact. Use the exact checksum string computed on the raw file bytes.

Technical quality metric summarizing the clarity of the raw spectral signal, measured from the raw file after acquisition and before interpretation. Typical values are instrument- and run-dependent; higher values indicate cleaner spectra.
Maximum observed intensity in the raw spectrum set, recorded as a technical summary of signal magnitude. Use instrument-native intensity units as stored in the file or export.

spectral_identification_processing.reasoning: For the spectral_identification_processing Process node, I included only computational processing parameters and software agent details: search engine name, version, repository, search database, enzyme rules, mass tolerances, scoring thresholds, and a processing-quality indicator. I excluded raw file properties, instrument settings, and identified interaction outputs because those belong to the Signal, Capture, and Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were supplied, so there were no overlaps to remove.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software package used to assign peptide and protein identifications from the raw spectra, recorded at the processing step. Example: MaxQuant, Mascot, Comet, Proteome Discoverer, MSFragger.

Version of the identification software used for spectral search and assignment, recorded exactly as run for this processing step. Include the full semantic version or release identifier when available.

Repository, package source, or distribution channel for the identification software used in this processing step, recorded to make the computational workflow reproducible. Examples include GitHub, vendor distribution, or package manager source.

Protein sequence database used for spectral identification, recorded at the time spectra are searched. Example databases include UniProt human/viral reference sets or custom host-virus concatenated databases.

Proteolytic enzyme specificity assumed by the search engine when identifying peptides from raw spectra, recorded as a processing parameter. Examples include trypsin, LysC, or semi-tryptic search settings.
Allowed precursor mass error for the spectral search, in parts per million, used at the time of identification processing. Typical values are often 5-20 ppm depending on instrument and method.
Allowed fragment ion mass error for the spectral search, in daltons, used at the time of identification processing. Typical values are often 0.01-0.6 Da depending on the analyzer and search strategy.
Target false discovery rate threshold applied during identification filtering, expressed as a percentage, measured at the end of the search and validation step. Common values are 1 or 5 percent.

Minimum score or confidence threshold required for peptide assignments to be retained by the processing pipeline, recorded as a software-specific cutoff. Use the numeric cutoff used in this experiment.
Method used by the software to infer proteins from peptide identifications, recorded at the processing step. Examples include parsimony, shared-peptide inference, or peptide-centric inference.

Qualitative indicator of whether the identification processing completed successfully and produced interpretable peptide/protein calls. Use this to flag software or search issues before downstream interaction interpretation.

identified_protein_interactions.reasoning: For the identified_protein_interactions Derivative node, I included only computed interaction-result descriptors: inference/score method, interaction confidence thresholds, output size, network-local result characteristics, and result quality. I excluded upstream raw spectra and search software parameters because those belong to Signal and Process nodes, and I excluded downstream network assembly details because those belong to the next Derivative/Process layer. No already_generated fields were provided, so I avoided only semantic territory overlaps.

md_schema.descr: Algorithm or rule used to infer virus-host protein interaction candidates from peptide and protein identifications, recorded at the point the derivative is computed. Examples include spectral-count enrichment, shared peptide association, or bait-prey scoring.

Minimum confidence or score required for an interaction candidate to be retained in the computed set, recorded after identification processing and before network assembly. Use the software-defined threshold or study-defined cutoff.

Primary numeric metric used to rank or support candidate virus-host interactions, for example confidence score, enrichment score, or posterior probability. Record the metric name or convention used by the derivative.
Total number of virus-host protein interaction candidates in the computed result set, counted after filtering by the chosen confidence criterion. This reflects the size of the derivative output.

Number of distinct viral proteins represented among the inferred interaction candidates, counted in the computed interaction set. This is a summary property of the derivative output, not of the source sample.
Number of distinct host proteins represented among the inferred interaction candidates, counted in the computed interaction set. This summarizes the derivative output after inference and filtering.

Whether the derived interactions are represented as directed or undirected in the computed candidate set, recorded after inference. Use this to describe the topology convention of the result table or structure.

Qualitative assessment of the computed interaction set, captured after inference and filtering. Use this to indicate whether the derived results appear complete, sparse, or dominated by low-confidence calls.

interaction_network_assembly.reasoning: For the interaction_network_assembly Process node, I included only network-construction and computation descriptors: software identity, version, repository, network model type, layout/assembly parameters, filtering or weighting rules, and a process-level quality flag. I excluded source interaction content and final network output properties because those belong to the identified_protein_interactions Derivative and the virus_host_interaction_network Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating software fields semantically already used for the spectral_identification_processing process by keeping this node focused on the network assembly software and its parameters, not the search engine details.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or workflow used to assemble identified virus-host interactions into a network representation, recorded at the network-assembly step. Example: Cytoscape, igraph, NetworkX, custom network analysis pipeline.
Version of the network assembly software used to construct the interaction network, recorded exactly as executed for this step. Include the full version string or release identifier when available.

Repository or distribution source for the network assembly software, recorded to support reproducibility of the downstream computation. Examples include GitHub, package manager source, or vendor distribution.

Graph representation generated from the identified interactions at assembly time, such as simple graph, bipartite graph, or directed multigraph. Record the structure used to organize viral and host proteins into a network.

Method used to assign weights or strengths to network edges during assembly, recorded at the computation step. Examples include confidence score propagation, spectral count weighting, or unweighted edges.

Criterion used to include or exclude proteins when assembling the interaction network, recorded during the network construction step. Examples include minimum interaction confidence, minimum degree, or presence in bait-specific subsets.

Layout algorithm used to arrange nodes for visualization or analysis during the assembly step, if a layout was computed as part of the process. Examples include force-directed, Fruchterman-Reingold, or Kamada-Kawai.

Qualitative indicator of whether the network assembly completed successfully and produced a coherent graph from the identified interactions. Use this to flag disconnected, malformed, or incomplete network construction results.

virus_host_interaction_network.reasoning: For the virus_host_interaction_network Derivative node, I included only properties of the computed network result: graph size, node and edge counts, network density, centrality summary, connected components, export format, and a result-quality flag. I excluded upstream assembly software and parameters because those belong to the interaction_network_assembly Process node, and I excluded raw interaction inference details because those belong to the identified_protein_interactions Derivative node. No already_generated fields were supplied, so I avoided only semantic overlap with nearby layers.

md_schema.descr: Digital representation format of the derived virus-host interaction network, recorded for the final computed result. Examples include graphml, gml, json, or edge list.
Total number of nodes in the derived virus-host interaction network, counted after assembly of the final graph. This summarizes the size of the output network object.
Total number of edges in the derived virus-host interaction network, counted after assembly of the final graph. Use the final exported graph edge count, not the intermediate interaction table size.
Density of the derived interaction network, computed as the proportion of observed edges to possible edges for the chosen graph representation. Typical values are between 0 and 1 for simple graphs.
Number of connected components in the derived virus-host interaction network, measured on the final graph. Use this to summarize whether the network is fragmented or cohesive.

Identifier of the node with the highest centrality or degree in the derived network, reported as the protein or protein group name used in the final graph. Record the most connected viral or host node if a single hub is defined.

Centrality score associated with the designated hub node in the derived network, recorded at the end of network analysis. Use the numeric score corresponding to the centrality metric chosen in this workflow.
Storage location or URI of the final derived network file, recorded after the network is assembled and exported. Examples include file paths, object store URIs, or database accessions.
Qualitative assessment of the final derived network, captured after assembly and export. Use this to indicate whether the graph is complete and interpretable for downstream antiviral target analysis.
